name: cloud-wiki
description: Cloud Wiki (#1778): a small encyclopedia of Markdown pages. No bottom nav: a collapsed left side menu (libs:ui-nav-bars vertical_side_menu) holds the topics in four groups, Sciences (Math, Computer Science, Physics, Astronomy, Engineering, Medicine), Humanities (Anthropology, Human Belief Systems, Chronos), Arts (Art, Theater, Music, Movies) and Explore (Graph), and each topic has its subpages as top tabs after an Overview tab (Engineering: one subpage per major field). A page is a short, neutral, educational Markdown explanation with tag chips; tapping a chip filters every page by that tag. Graph is an Obsidian-style force-directed graph (libs:graph-view, shared with Cloud Notes) joining pages by their [[links]] and shared tags, with pan, zoom and tap to open. The content is the runtime dataset wiki (data/fleet/app/com.diegonmarcos.cloudwiki/wiki.json) served by Cloud Store, never an APK asset. Configs are the fleet's General | Perms | About. Declares no network permission of its own. #1789 Chronos also holds the interactive simulators of diegonmarcos/lib-chronos: one nested page per Chronos page of the repo, in its hierarchy and with its titles, shown in the fleet web view (libs:web-core, APP_PAGE) and served offline from APK assets (assets/chronos, WebViewAssetLoader on the asset origin; every other request is answered 403). They are baked at build time from a pinned commit (tools/chronos-pin.json, tools/regen-chronos.py, drift-checked by test/test-chronos.sh), the one exception to the runtime dataset.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.
auto_update._doc_enabled: Off because this app compiles no libs:updater: the Store updates it, as it does Cloud Calc and Cloud Search.

ui._doc: #868 THE nav declaration (libs:bottomnav NavDecl) of Cloud Wiki. ui.bottom_nav is EMPTY: the app has no bottom nav (owner request, declared in nav-shape.json::no_bottom). The pages are the ONE section `wiki`, default_section, drawn in vertical_side_menu mode (the collapsed rail; libs:ui-nav-bars NavSectionLayout) with four groups. Each topic page has its subpages as top tabs (the runtime dataset wiki.json, topics[id].pages), after an Overview tab; the Graph page draws every page as a node. test-wiki-app.sh holds the topic ids in step with the dataset both ways. #1789 the Chronos page holds NESTED pages (written by tools/regen-chronos.py from lib-chronos at the pin, never typed): one per index.html of the repo's Chronos/ tree, in its hierarchy, label = the page's <title>, `asset` = its file under assets/chronos (Decl.chronos reads it; NavDecl ignores the key). The side menu indents them under Chronos and the title dropdown lists them, so the nav walk covers them; test-chronos.sh C1 holds the declaration equal to the baked tree.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: A small encyclopedia with a graph
about.description: Cloud Wiki is a small encyclopedia of short, neutral, educational pages in thirteen topics. A collapsed side menu groups the topics, each topic has its subpages as top tabs, every page carries tag chips that filter the whole wiki, and the Graph page joins pages by their links and shared tags. The pages are served at runtime by Cloud Store; nothing else is baked into the app but the Chronos simulators, which run offline from the app's own copy of the lib-chronos repository.
features: Sciences: Math, Computer Science, Physics, Astronomy, Engineering, Medicine
Humanities: Anthropology, Human Belief Systems, Chronos
Tag chips that filter every page
Graph: force-directed, pan, zoom, tap to open
Chronos simulators: every page of the lib-chronos repository, interactive, offline, in its own hierarchy

screens.name: Topic
screens.what: Overview and one tab per subpage, Markdown with tag chips.

screens.name: Tags
screens.what: Pick chips to list every page that carries them.

screens.name: Graph
screens.what: Pages as nodes, joined by links and shared tags.

screens.name: Chronos simulator
screens.what: A lib-chronos page in a web view, its sub-pages as tabs; links inside it move the menu along.

guide: Open the side menu for a topic.
Pick a subpage tab at the top.
Tap a tag chip to filter, a node in the graph to open its page.
Open Chronos in the side menu, then a simulator below it.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. The pages are read from Cloud Store's local data provider; the app contacts no server itself.

related.why: Opens this app from Cloud > Apps > Projects.
Installs and updates this app and serves its pages.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
